```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 3.8)
fmt <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
```

# Goodness-of-fit calibration

The martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family (`gof_univariate()`,
`gof_global()`, `gof_auxiliary()`, `martingale_residuals()`) reports p-values
against an analytic null. This article measures the type-I error of
`gof_univariate()` under correct specification: simulate from a model, fit the
**same** model, and collect the p-values. For a calibrated test they are
Uniform(0, 1), so the rejection rate at level α equals α.

**Settings.** A 20-actor one-mode network, the Gillespie simulator, 1,500
events, one control per case (the design the GoF uses), and 600 replicates per
cell. With 600 replicates the Monte Carlo standard error of a rejection rate
near 0.05 is about 0.009.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(amorem)
library(parallel)
actors <- paste0("a", 1:20)

# one replicate under correct specification: simulate with a known effect,
# fit the same linear model, return the gof_univariate p-value
gof_rep <- function(i, beta, stat, half_life = NULL) {
  set.seed(70000L + i)
  ev <- simulate_relational_events(
    n_events = 1500, senders = actors, receivers = actors,
    endogenous_stats = stat, endogenous_effects = setNames(beta, stat),
    half_life = half_life, method = "gillespie")
  gof_univariate(ev, model = setNames("linear", stat), covariate = stat,
                 half_life = half_life, seed = 90000L + i)$p_value
}

cells <- list(
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.0),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.1),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.2),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.3),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.5),
  list(stat = "recency", beta = 0.2),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_exp_decay", beta = 0.2, half_life = 5))
p <- lapply(cells, function(g) unlist(mclapply(1:600, gof_rep, beta = g$beta,
          stat = g$stat, half_life = g$half_life, mc.cores = 8)))
```

The p-values from that run (amorem 1.1.0) are stored with this article, and the
table and figure below are computed from them.

```{r results}
res <- readRDS("data/gof-calibration.rds")
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(res, list(res$stat, res$beta), drop = TRUE),
  function(d) data.frame(
    statistic     = d$stat[1],
    true_beta     = d$beta[1],
    replicates    = sum(!is.na(d$p_value)),
    reject_05     = mean(d$p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    reject_10     = mean(d$p_value < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    ks_uniformity = suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(stats::na.omit(d$p_value),
                                                    "punif")$p.value))))
tab <- tab[order(tab$statistic != "reciprocity_count", tab$statistic, tab$true_beta), ]
rownames(tab) <- NULL
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 1, 0, 3, 3, 4))
```

```{r results-numbers, include = FALSE}
cnt <- tab[tab$statistic == "reciprocity_count", ]
rec <- tab[tab$statistic == "recency", ]
dec <- tab[tab$statistic == "reciprocity_exp_decay", ]
mcse <- sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / 600)
```

```{r ecdf, fig.alt = "Empirical CDF of GoF p-values against the uniform diagonal"}
show <- list(c("reciprocity_count", 0.2), c("reciprocity_exp_decay", 0.2),
             c("recency", 0.2))
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
for (s in show) {
  pv <- sort(res$p_value[res$stat == s[1] & res$beta == as.numeric(s[2])])
  plot(pv, seq_along(pv) / length(pv), type = "s", lwd = 2, col = "#1f5fb4",
       xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "p-value", ylab = "empirical CDF",
       main = sprintf("%s, beta = %s", s[1], s[2]), cex.main = 0.9)
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
}
par(op)
```

## Reading the results

- **Count statistic.** For `reciprocity_count` the rejection rate at the 5%
  level ranges from `r fmt(min(cnt$reject_05))` to `r fmt(max(cnt$reject_05))`
  across true effects from 0 to 0.5, at most
  `r formatC(max(abs(cnt$reject_05 - 0.05)) / mcse, format = "f", digits = 1)`
  Monte Carlo standard errors (`r fmt(mcse)`) from 0.05. The p-value distribution is not exactly
  uniform in every cell: the uniformity test gives p =
  `r fmt(cnt$ks_uniformity[cnt$true_beta == 0.1], 4)` at β = 0.1 and p =
  `r formatC(cnt$ks_uniformity[cnt$true_beta == 0.5], format = "e", digits = 1)`
  at β = 0.5, while the rejection rate at 5% stays at nominal.
- **Decayed statistic.** `reciprocity_exp_decay` rejects at
  `r fmt(dec$reject_05)` (uniformity p = `r fmt(dec$ks_uniformity)`).
- **Recency.** `recency` rejects at `r fmt(rec$reject_05)`, which is
  `r formatC((rec$reject_05 - 0.05) / mcse, format = "f", digits = 1)` Monte
  Carlo standard errors above 0.05 (uniformity p =
  `r formatC(rec$ks_uniformity, format = "e", digits = 1)`).

## Guidance

- For count and decayed statistics, the p-values can be used at the 5% level in
  settings like these.
- For `recency`, the test rejects a correct model more often than the nominal
  level (`r fmt(rec$reject_05)` at 5%); read its p-value together with the
  cumulative residual process and `martingale_residuals()`.
- These cells cover one network size, one sample size and one control per case.
  The rejection rate as the number of controls grows has not been measured.

See the [Estimation](estimation.html) guide for the GoF API and
[Validation experiments](validation-experiments.html) for the recovery and
parity studies (E1–E7).
